 Coach Erik Spoelstra 's Miami Heat got a chance to face a familiar face as Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks invaded the Kaseya Center as Andrew Wiggins' unexpected role was discussed . Heat fans called out Tyler Herro for a strange reason as he returned to face the team that traded him for the first time.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The former Heat guard and current Bucks guard wore number eleven as he was introduced to some cheers and some boos, with more reactions falling into the former category.
 The Heat jumped out to a 44-28 lead early in the second quarter as Bam Adebayo and Klay Thompson combined for 25 points. Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Heat's superstar acquired from Milwaukee, had just two points through nine minutes of play as Herro sought to perform in front of the team that trained him in the NBA game.
 Herro had four points through 12 minutes of action, shooting 2-of-6 for the field in an underwhelming return near the eight-minute mark of the second quarter.
 Click Here to Subscribe Herro spoke about a strained relationship with his former teammate Adebayo before the game, saying that things change fast. The ultra competitive NBA atmosphere favored Spoelstra's Heat as Taylor Jenkins ' team didn't seem to have enough firepower to strike back at the duo of Thompson and Adebayo on the offensive end.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Herro will always be remembered for his magical playoff runs in a Heat uniform, but Miami got a princely sum in return for him. The Heat now have bigger and better goals while the Bucks tried to fight back to respectability with a 1-13 record in danger of going 1-14.
